description: Sitting Kegel guide: a discreet pelvic-floor squeeze on a chair, at a desk or in a car, how it should feel, common mistakes, easier and harder versions.
intro: The sitting Kegel is the same lift and squeeze, done upright on a chair. It is the easiest version to fit into daily life: at a desk, on a bus or at a red light, nobody notices. Sitting adds a little more load than lying, and the seat gives useful feedback.
feel: Sitting on your sit bones, you should feel the area between them draw up and away from the seat, then settle back as you relax. Your glutes stay soft, so you do not rise on the chair. Keep breathing and keep your shoulders loose. Pushing down or a stiff neck means the squeeze is too hard.

mistakes.right: Sit tall on your sit bones, feet flat. A slouched pelvis makes the squeeze harder to find and to release.

mistakes.wrong: Rising off the seat by clenching your buttocks
mistakes.right: If your body lifts, that was your glutes. Keep seat contact the same and look for a smaller, internal lift.

mistakes.wrong: Squeezing every time you sit down
mistakes.right: Link a few sets to fixed moments, like traffic lights or finishing emails. Constant squeezing can leave the muscles tense.

easier: Use 2 to 3 second holds, or sit slightly reclined with your back supported. If you feel nothing, return to the lying version.
harder: Lengthen the hold while breathing normally, or perch on the front edge of the chair. Finish with a few quick squeezes.
who: Desk workers, drivers and commuters, and people over 50 who find getting down to the floor harder.
skip: If your pelvic floor already feels tight, or you have pain when sitting or with sex, focus on relaxing first and see a pelvic floor physiotherapist. Never let practice pull your attention from the road. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Can you do Kegels at your desk?
faq.a: Yes. Sit tall, feet flat, and do a slow set while breathing normally. Linking it to a regular task makes it an easy habit.

faq.q: Is it safe to do Kegels while driving?
faq.a: A few gentle reps at a red light are fine for most people. Skip it if it distracts you.
